clues: A river cuts right through the middle of this city, bending in a big S as it goes. Two parts of town face each other across the water.
Spring and fall here are mild and warm, with plenty of rain. Thunderstorms rumble through often in those seasons.
In 1792, when the state joined the Union, this small town was picked. Five men from five parts of the state made the pick.
This city got its name from a river crossing. In 1780, a pioneer was killed in a fight at the ford, and people named the crossing for him.
The governor of Kentucky works in this town by the river. The men and women who make state laws meet in the capitol here.
